messages.text: Hamilton calls for 'serious talks' at Ferrari after Leclerc incident

metadata.summary: Lewis Hamilton has called for "serious talks" at Ferrari after his opening lap incident with Charles Leclerc at the Mexico City Grand Prix, while team principal Frederic Vasseur suggested there was not enough "respect" given.
metadata.content: Lewis Hamilton demands 'serious talks' at Ferrari after Charles Leclerc incident at Mexico City Grand Prix | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Lewis Hamilton demands 'serious talks' at Ferrari after Charles Leclerc incident at Mexico City Grand Prix Lewis Hamilton reiterated "something needs to change" after his latest incident with Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc cost the Scuderia victory in Mexico; watch Friday's practice sessions in Brazil from 3.30pm and 7pm, live on Sky Sports F1 Tuesday 3 November 2026 06:10, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Martin Brundle feels Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc's squabbling during the Mexico City GP cost them a one-two finish Lewis Hamilton has called for "serious talks" at Ferrari after his opening lap incident with Charles Leclerc at the Mexico City Grand Prix, while team principal Frederic Vasseur suggested there was not enough "respect" given. Leclerc attacked Hamilton around the outside going into Turn 4 but outbraked himself and cut the corner to take the lead, while Hamilton lost out to Red Bull's Max Verstappen after briefly going off track. The stewards gave Leclerc a five-second time penalty which allowed Verstappen to overtake him during the pit stop phase, going on to win the race while Hamilton finished second and Leclerc in fourth. metadata.summary: George Russell has posted a statement on social media to "speak from the heart" after his Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli secured the F1 Drivers' Championship on Sunday.
metadata.content: George Russell: Mercedes driver posts statement to 'speak from the heart' after Kimi Antonelli becomes world champion at Mexico City Grand Prix | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content George Russell: Mercedes driver posts statement to 'speak from the heart' after Kimi Antonelli becomes world champion at Mexico City Grand Prix Mercedes' George Russell took to social media on Monday after not speaking to the media after Sunday's Mexico City GP, where his team-mate Kimi Antonelli became world champion; watch Friday's practice sessions for the Sao Paulo GP at 3.30pm and 7pm, live on Sky Sports F1 Monday 2 November 2026 20:31, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Martin Brundle believes Kimi Antonelli winning the world title could trigger an 'overdrive' for George Russell, or it's 'game over' for the Mercedes team-mate George Russell has posted a statement on social media to "speak from the heart" after his Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli secured the F1 Drivers' Championship on Sunday. Mercedes boss Toto Wolff revealed Russell was "distraught" in Mexico and went home after congratulating Antonelli on becoming world champion. The FIA gave Mercedes a €5,000 (£4,173) fine as Russell missed his mandatory media duties post-race, but the British driver has made his own first public comments on Monday. messages.text: Bears make statement against champion Seahawks

metadata.summary: Caleb Williams threw a touchdown pass on the opening drive and Jeffery Simmons delivered just what Chicago needed on defense as the Bears beat the Seattle Seahawks 34-17 on Monday night.
metadata.content: Chicago Bears deliver statement win over Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks as Caleb Williams and Jeffery Simmons star | NFL News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Chicago Bears deliver statement win over Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks as Caleb Williams and Jeffery Simmons star Jeffery Simmons stars on his debut for the Chicago Bears against the Seattle Seahawks in his first appearance since arriving in a blockbuster trade from the Tennessee Titans; watch the 2026 NFL season live on Sky Sports, including every minute of the playoffs Tuesday 3 November 2026 06:38, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the Week 8 matchup between the Seattle Seahawks and the Chicago Bears Caleb Williams threw a touchdown pass on the opening drive and Jeffery Simmons delivered just what Chicago needed on defense as the Bears beat the Seattle Seahawks 34-17 on Monday night. Williams was extremely efficient for the Bears (6-2) against one of the NFL's stingiest defenses, committing no turnovers, taking just one sack and throwing for 247 yards while completing 71 per cent of his passes. Williams' play helped set up three short touchdown runs by D'Andre Swift and that proved to be more than enough against Sam Darnold and the Seahawks (4-4), thanks to the impact Simmons had on the defense.
